## NBA buzz: Latest on trades, news, roster moves and intel for the 2026-27 season

The league is in full swing, and the transaction wire isn't slowing down. ESPN's insider team continues to track the latest moves, whispers and personnel developments as front offices navigate the early stretch of the 2026-27 campaign. It's the kind of around-the-clock coverage that becomes essential when rosters are still taking shape and the rumor mill never stops turning. Bookmark this space—it's your running ledger of what's happening behind the scenes and on the books across all 30 franchises.

## NBA Rookie Rankings: 10 standouts in a star-studded class

The 2026 draft class is living up to the hype. ESPN's Zach Kram has compiled the first edition of rookie rankings for the season, spotlighting 10 first-year players who've separated themselves in the early going. This isn't a weak crop by any measure—the talent pool runs deep, and the names making noise right now suggest we're watching the beginning of several long, productive careers. It's early, sure, but these 10 have already shown enough to warrant attention as the class takes its first real steps at the NBA level.

## Castle helps Spurs stay unbeaten on road with 123-107 win over Kings minus Wemby, Fox and Harper

Stephon Castle put together a monster line—28 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds—as the San Antonio Spurs cruised past the Sacramento Kings 123-107 on Monday night. The win keeps San Antonio perfect away from home, a remarkable feat made even more impressive by the absence of Victor Wembanyama. The Kings, meanwhile, were without key pieces of their own in De'Aaron Fox and Ron Harper Jr., but Castle made sure there was no drama down the stretch. It was the kind of complete performance that underscores how much the Spurs can lean on their young guard when their franchise centerpiece sits.
